# Instruments: SFZ sample libraries

Use muser's built-in SFZ sampler (manguebyte-sampler) to play `.sfz` sound libraries, with no external plugin needed.

```json
{ "name": "piano", "instrument": "sfz:/path/to/Piano.sfz", "clips": [ ... ] }
```

- Syntax: `sfz:<path to the .sfz file>`; sample files are read from the .sfz file's directory by the relative paths in the .sfz (WAV, FLAC and others are supported).
- The path can be absolute or relative to a sound library (such as `sfz:SalamanderGrandPiano-SFZ+FLAC-V3+20200602/SalamanderGrandPiano-V3+20200602.sfz`):
  a relative path is looked up in the environment variable `MUSER_SFZ_PATH` (the root directories of sound libraries, separated by `:`, or `;` on Windows), and subdirectories up to two levels below a root are searched too,
  so that the same project works on different machines. For shared projects prefer relative paths.
- A note's `pitch` is a MIDI pitch; the range, velocity layers, loops and release samples are all defined by the .sfz file. Up to 32 voices at once.
- Large sound libraries whose sample files total more than 1 GB are streamed from disk automatically (memory keeps only the start and loop section of each sample); the sound is the same as reading everything in, but rendering is several times slower; smaller libraries are read entirely into memory.
- `muser validate` checks that the .sfz file exists; missing samples or format errors are reported at render time.
- Supported expressive opcodes: filters (`fil_type` `cutoff` `resonance` `fil_keytrack` `fil_veltrack`) and filter envelopes (`fileg_*`);
  `<opcode>_onccN` modulated **in real time** by controllers (volume, pan, pitch, cutoff, resonance, each stage of the two envelopes), with controller values taken from the project's
  `instrument_params.cc`, or from the .sfz's `set_ccN` when not written. `amplitude_onccN` is multiplicative by SFZ convention, and is folded into a fixed amplitude at load time using the controller value.
  Velocity crossfades (`xfin_lovel` etc.) and the velocity curve `amp_velcurve_N` are approximated by splitting by velocity (one segment per 8 levels); `*noise` white noise
  and a `#include` on the same line after the header can also be read.
- Unsupported ones (LFOs `lfoN_*` `amplfo_*` etc., pitch envelopes `pitcheg_*`, `offset_random`, `<curve>`, `<effect>`, region EQ `eqN_*` etc.)
  are listed with their names and counts on stderr at render time, and the sound may differ slightly from the original design (for example, no vibrato).
- `instrument_params` supports two items (applied at load time, cannot be automated):
  - `"cc": { "105": 127 }`: set controller values. Many sound libraries use controllers as switches (mono mode, string choice, unison volume, filter, vibrato depth...),
    and muser selects regions by these values (`loccN`/`hiccN`) and folds in `volume_onccN` / `amplitude_onccN` / `pan_onccN`;
    controllers not given use the default of `set_ccN` in the .sfz.
  - `"keyswitch": "Staccato"`: choose the articulation of a keyswitch (`sw_last`); it can be an `sw_label` name, a pitch number or a note name; the default is `sw_default`.
  - `muser instruments "sfz:/path/to.sfz"` lists the controllers this sound declares (names and defaults) and the selectable articulations.
- Triggering works as the .sfz designs it: `trigger=first` / `legato` (legato samples, triggered while the previous key is still held; write `"legato": true` on a clip to connect them automatically,
  see the legato section of SKILLS.md), `release` (release tails when a key is released / the pedal is lifted, string resonance).
- For anything else to adjust, add effects on the track (such as `eq`, `reverb`).
- Vibrato and vibrato depth are often controlled by CC1 (mod wheel): `instrument_params: { "cc": { "1": 64 } }` opens it halfway, and 0 turns it off.
- Free sound libraries: freepats (piano, guitar, etc.), Versilian VSCO (orchestral), sfzinstruments.github.io.
- The path is a path on this machine; after moving the project to another machine, change it to the new location.
- For piano-type sounds with the sustain pedal: the clip's `pedal` field, see [pedal.md](../pedal.md).
